newsitem.title: INDIA: India industry poll shows praise for government.
newsitem.headline: India industry poll shows praise for government.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's 10-month-old government has won good marks from industry leaders for its efforts to promote economic reforms, a poll conducted by Business Standard newspaper said on Monday.
Ten industry leaders were polled after the Congress party on Sunday withdrew its crucial support for Deve Gowda's United Front coalition and plunged the nation into a political crisis.
Two of the leaders rated the government 5.0 on a scale of 10, four gave it 6.0, one 7.0, one 7.5 and two 8.0.

"The economy has done well under the 10-month-old government, which gave it a renewed thrust to reforms," K.V. Kamath, head of Industrial Credit and Information Corporation of India (ICICI), said. He rated the government 8.0.
The coalition, which bands free-marketeers, communists and regional groups, has done well despite constraints, they said.

"Considering that the government was constrained in making decisions, its performance was not bad; it has been moderate," said Harsh Goenka, vice-chairman of RPG Enterprises. He rated the government a six.

Finance Minister P. Chidambaram's 1997/98 (April-March) budget, which slashed import tariffs and corporate tax rates, was hailed by the business leaders. The proposals were scheduled to be considered by parliament after it reconvenes on April 21.
"The highlight of the regime was the (recent) budget, which was excellent," said Nimesh Kampani, chairman of JM Financial, who gave the government a score of 5.0.
But "it has also put some major decisions on hold," he said, referring to the qustion of whether or not to raise the prices of petroleum products to bridge a deficit linked to fuel prices.
Business leaders and brokers told Reuters on Sunday their main concern was whether parliament would approve the budget.

The United Front took bold initiatives on disinvestment of state company shares, simplification of company law, setting up a telecommunications industry regulator and working out an agreement with the central bank to phase out inflation-causing ad-hoc treasury bills, the polled leaders said.
"However, the domestic industry could have gained much had the budget been passed," said Shekhar Dutta, president of Confederation of Indian Industry. He rated the government 7.5.
